title: Compute brief - 13 November 2026
description: Buyers are paying for power before they sign leases. Fermi got a $200 million prepayment from an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler for 600 MW at Project Matador while its TensorWave lease died, Cerebras signed Microsoft but says new capacity only ramps from December, and NAVER sold 20 MW to a US inference company for about $1.5 billion. Wire: Fermi, Cerebras, NAVER, Australia cancellations and CDC 1.4 GW filing, Kazakhstan Gcore MoU. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
lede: The day after Nvidia lost its founder-CEO, the clearest signal came from buyers paying for power before they sign leases. Fermi said an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler agreed a $200 million prepayment and a $15 million early-works deal to advance 600 MW at Project Matador in Texas from 2027, with no lease yet; the same release said Fermi's August lease with AMD-backed TensorWave is terminated. Cerebras signed Microsoft as its third hyperscaler customer and has 700 MW under contract, but expects cloud revenue to stay flat this quarter because new capacity only starts ramping in December. NAVER sold 20 MW of 2027 capacity to a US inference company for about 2 trillion won ($1.5 billion). On Nvidia, Reuters reports interim CEO Colette Kress pushed back on Huang's large financing deals, including investments in OpenAI and Lambda, that a proposed $250 billion plan to support OpenAI's Ohio project was pared to $120 billion, and that the stock fell as much as 14% on Thursday before closing down 4.3%. List prices held for a fifth straight day: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $4.59 and B200 at $7.69.
